item.title: Okayama Castle: The Black Crow Castle — Guide
item.description: Okayama Castle is known as Ujo, the Crow Castle, for the striking black lacquered boards that clad its walls — a deliberate contrast to the white ‘White Heron’ castle at Himeji. Originally completed in 1597 by Ukita Hideie, it stood on the bank of the Asahi River, which served as its natural moat, until the keep was destroyed in a wartime air raid in 1945. The present keep is a 1966 reconstruction, extensively renewed in 2022, housing a well-presented museum of the castle and its lords, with a top-floor view over the river to Korakuen garden directly opposite.
